status: exact compact equilibrium and converged Fokker-Planck relaxation spectrum; the stochastic-time gap rescales with mobility and is not a physical transfer gap

compactModel.configuration: theta in U(1), theta modulo 2 pi
compactModel.langevin: d theta_s=-M beta sin(theta_s) ds+sqrt(2M) dW_s
compactModel.fokkerPlanck: partial_s P=M partial_theta(partial_theta P+beta sin(theta) P)

selfAdjointTransform.factorization: H_FP=M A_dagger A with A=d_theta+(beta/2) sin(theta)
selfAdjointTransform.fourierMatrix: diag n^2+beta^2/8; distance-one entries -beta/4; distance-two entries -beta^2/16, all multiplied by M

mobilityAudit.constantMobility: H_FP(M)=M H_FP(1), so every nonzero relaxation eigenvalue and the stochastic-time gap scale exactly with M
mobilityAudit.timeRescaling: s'=M s removes a constant M without changing the equilibrium distribution
mobilityAudit.stateDependentMobility: positive m(theta) gives H=A_dagger m(theta) A and preserves the same ground state while generally changing nonzero eigenvalue ratios
mobilityAudit.conclusion: the relaxation gap is algorithmic/dynamical data of the chosen stochastic process, not an invariant of the equilibrium Euclidean measure

physicalComparison.reasonForChoice: a compact quantum rotor with the same coordinate and cosine potential, but physical-time kinetic dynamics
physicalComparison.comparisonRule: its gap is independent of stochastic mobility M and is not equal to the M-dependent Fokker-Planck relaxation gap
physicalComparison.warning: the supersymmetric-quantum-mechanics interpretation of H_FP does not turn fictitious Parisi-Wu time into the physical Euclidean time already contained in the field coordinate

fourDimensionalRequirements.existence: construct the gauge-field stochastic process globally for the regulator and control its continuum limit
fourDimensionalRequirements.ergodicity: prove convergence to a unique equilibrium for gauge-invariant observables, including topology and flat gauge directions
fourDimensionalRequirements.gaugeHandling: control gauge-orbit diffusion or stochastic gauge fixing without changing gauge-invariant equilibrium observables
fourDimensionalRequirements.equilibriumIdentification: prove that the stationary measure is the intended Yang-Mills Euclidean measure nonperturbatively
fourDimensionalRequirements.reflectionPositivity: establish Osterwalder-Schrader positivity and reconstruction in physical Euclidean time at equilibrium
fourDimensionalRequirements.physicalGap: prove a positive lower spectral bound for the reconstructed physical Hamiltonian, not for the stochastic generator
fourDimensionalRequirements.uniformity: make existence, mixing/equilibrium, locality and physical spectral estimates uniform as volume grows and cutoff is removed

topologyAndCriticalSlowing.finiteRegulator: compact finite lattices can define well-behaved link diffusions, but mixing constants may deteriorate
topologyAndCriticalSlowing.continuumRisk: topological-sector tunneling and long physical correlation lengths can drive the stochastic relaxation gap to zero
topologyAndCriticalSlowing.logicalLesson: even a uniform stochastic mixing gap would be mobility-dependent and would not by itself be the Yang-Mills mass gap

spin23Boundary.useful: stochastic quantization may sample a compact internal gauge measure used in a Spin(2,3)-adjacent construction
spin23Boundary.notABridge: Spin(2,3) does not identify fictitious stochastic time with physical time or transfer a mobility-dependent Fokker-Planck gap into a gauge-invariant particle mass

decision: Stochastic quantization correctly recovers the compact equilibrium measure in the witness, but its relaxation gap scales with an arbitrary mobility/time convention and differs from a physical rotor gap. A four-dimensional route must construct and identify the equilibrium Yang-Mills measure, prove physical-time OS reconstruction and then prove the reconstructed Hamiltonian gap uniformly in regulator limits.
